messages:
maya: heads-up — we're seeing an eviction spike in eu-west1 starting ~22:10 UTC, mostly tiny inference pods (0.25/0.5 GPU) getting repeatedly preempted :eyes:
rory: noticed that too, graph shows evictions +230% vs 1h baseline, overall GPU idle slots at ~18% but fragmented in small pockets
liam: can you paste a sample node dump? suspecting lease/heartbeat mismatch again
maya: `kubectl describe node gpu-eu-west1-03` showed a bunch of pods Pending with `InsufficientGPU` but node allocatable says free fractional slots
---
maya: here's an example snippet:
```
Allocated: 0.5/4 GPUs
Available tiny slots: 3 x 0.25 (but tagged as leased by scheduler-leasesvc)
lease-holder: scheduler-lease-72f
lease-last-heartbeat: 2024-11-03T22:09:08Z
```
rory: that lease-last-heartbeat is old — lease-sweeper hasn't reclaimed some leases after node reboot
liam: any recent changes to lease timeouts or node-restart handling?
anika: we rolled a tiny lease optimization last week to avoid noisy reclamation (increased lease TTL from 60->300s) to reduce churning for long-running tiny jobs
maya: seems that backfired in reprovision scenarios — when a node goes into REPAIR state leases linger and scheduler can't see true free slots so it packs larger pods elsewhere -> cascade of evictions
jamie: log from lease-sweeper: `WARN reclaimable leases=12 node-not-ready=true sweep_errors=3`
rory: network blips in eu-west1 AZ-B at 21:58 caused several nodes to transiently mark NotReady, leases stayed sticky
liam: immediate mitigations: 1) lower lease TTL back to 90s for eu-west1 canary 2) run a one-off aggressive sweep to free stuck leases 3) enable temporary backfill packing for tiny pods (pack-unreserved=true)
anika: lowering TTL increases churn risk, but agree as short-term emergency canary. Will open a PR to flip flag for eu-west1 only.
maya: ops request: can SRE run the one-off sweep and monitor evictions for 15m?
jamie: @sre-bot can you schedule `lease-sweeper --dry=false --aggressive` in eu-west1 now? :pray:
sre-bot: scheduled job lease-sweeper-eu-west1-500123 at 2024-11-03T22:25:40Z. Notifying owners.
liam: also propose a small scheduler heuristic: allow fractional-slot compaction for tiny-pods to prefer co-locating into partially used nodes when fragmentation>12%
rory: that requires simulator validation — can we run replay with last 24h trace?
anika: will run the trace job on staging; if compaction reduces evictions in sim by >15% we'll canary change in eu-west1
maya: cost note — current fragmentation is causing extra cross-AZ placements and bumping egress/cold-warm remainder costs ~+7% on that fleet. need to include in postmortem
jamie: agree, tag finance with a quick note. also verify Dedicated capacity customers not impacted by the sweep
liam: for Dedicated we must exclude nodes labeled `dedicated=true` from aggressive sweep, will add guard in job
rory: timeline: do sweep now, rollback lease TTL if no regressions by 22:40, run simulator by 23:10, canary compaction flag if sim looks good
anika: PR up in 2m: https://git.internal/redwood/lease-service/pulls/1234 (eu-west1 TTL canary)
maya: thanks. i'll keep posting short updates here. tagging @liam for the compaction sim results. :thumbsup:
jamie: ping if we need to throttle API ingress, might be wise if evictions worsen
sre-bot: sweep job completed: reclaimed 14 leases, errors=0, reclaimed_nodes=9, run_time=22s
maya: quick check — evictions dropped to baseline within 4m. Allocatable tiny slots now usable
liam: good signal. still need to validate compaction sim before changing scheduler default
rory: postmortem checklist: root cause (long TTL + node NotReady race), immediate mitigation (aggressive sweep + TTL canary), follow-ups (sim, compaction heuristic, exclude dedicated nodes, add observability metric lease-staleness)
anika: adding ticket to eng-platform backlog: EP-4821 "lease-staleness dashboard + compaction sim"
maya: wrapping up here — thanks all :heart:
jamie: nice fast run. :shipit:
